static_traits.name: Lin Anxi
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with the audience and fellow musicians are strained by self-criticism
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem history; not yet received counseling before; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear logic, can describe experiences and feelings concretely; tone of anxiety and self-criticism coexisting; skeptical of others' praise; high cooperativeness, willing to try suggestions

basic_info.main_problem: I am troubled by the sense of failure and disappointment from my last music performance; despite overall positive feedback, I cannot shake the feeling that the final section was not good enough.
basic_info.core_demands: I realized these feelings of failure have affected my mental health and my passion for music, so I sought counseling.

special_situations.event: A few mistakes appeared in the final performance segment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes in key passages, the whole performance is a failure, and I do not deserve to be a musician
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying in my mind and harshly self-criticizing, ignoring positive feedback

special_situations.event: Receives positive evaluations from friends and audiences after the performance ends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' praise is unreliable, possibly just politeness or comfort
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, continuously focusing on error details
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; the truth is I performed very badly

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If similar mistakes happen again, my reputation will be ruined, and I do not deserve to keep making music
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids listening back to recordings; sinks into worry and rehearsing failure scenes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess up next time too

special_situations.event: When recalling the whole performance, only staring at the error clips
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only a performance completely without mistakes counts as success
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Filters out successful episodes, focusing only on shortcomings to 'maintain standards'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The good parts do not count, what matters is I made mistakes

core_conflict.wish: Longing for sincere recognition from audience and peers, maintaining perfect performance and good reputation
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and being negated, worried about reputation damage, seen as not good enough
defense_goal: Avoids failure and shame through harsh self-demands and self-criticism
Staying skeptical of praise to avoid 'being fooled' or negated
Avoiding situations that may expose shortcomings (like listening back to recordings) to ease anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: A musician prone to mistakes who needs to prove herself (self-critic)
object_relations.object_representation: Picky and possibly insincere audience / others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends or audiences give positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client sees the other as perfunctory or insincere (projecting her own negation experience onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone gentle and inquiring, invites them to distinguish facts from speculation, concretize the evidence sources of others' feedback, and encourages examining the details of actual interactions with the other party.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests recording playback or practicing the final section in a low-pressure environment
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client worries this will 'prove she is terrible', imagining the worst outcome in advance to cope with uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a supportive, empathic tone, negotiating small-step experiments (short time, safe environment), focusing first on neutral and positive cues, setting controllable observation dimensions to lower emotional activation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When alone, repeatedly recalls the erroneous segments in the performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing one mistake as a negation of overall self-worth, aggression turned against the self
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using high empathy and embodied language, naming self-attack, turning judgment into concrete improvable behavior items, guiding practice of self-compassion and balanced evaluation.

manifestations: Relationships with the audience and fellow musicians are strained by self-criticism
Mainly relying on mother as the only emotional support
Lacking trust in others' praise, hard to build genuine connections
Strongly ties self-worth to perfection and reputation
The sense of failure overshadows the love of and experience with music itself

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Believing 'only a performance without mistakes counts as success'
Emphasizes 'must impress the audience and maintain reputation' to demand of himself

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'
manifestations: Attributing her own negation experience to others' 'insincere praise'
Questioning the sincerity of others' praise

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly replaying mistake clips in one's head
Worrying upcoming performances will be ruined
Daring not to listen back to recordings

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling her performance after shows, the client usually focuses only on mistakes, negating overall achievement, and sinks into failure and anxiety, further worrying about upcoming performances.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In that performance, the opening and several improvisational segments were natural and fluent; the client experienced smoothness and a sense of control on the spot and obtained positive feedback from friends and audience, contrasting with their dominant narrative that 'the whole thing was a disaster'.
exception_events.reason: Different support: positive feedback from friends and audience on site; different situation: better-prepared opening, lower-pressure improvisation; different approach: focusing more on the musical experience itself than self-judgment at the time.

positive_force: Friends' and audiences' positive feedback and recognition
Having solid performance and stage ability (overall positive evaluation of the whole show, natural opening and improvisation)
Can identify and name her own highlights (like acknowledging a good opening)
negative_force: Significant tendencies toward catastrophizing and mental filtering
Negating positive feedback and mind-reading inferences about others' motives
Predictive worries and self-criticism about upcoming performances leading to relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly replaying mistakes after shows and negating overall performance, with marked anxiety and failure
antecedent: Recalling the whole performance after it
When receiving positive evaluations from others
Thinking of upcoming performances and reputation
target_behavior.core_reason: To maintain perfection and reputation, equating key-passage mistakes with total failure, catastrophic thinking driving harsh self-criticism and distrust of praise
target_behavior.function: Using harsh self-monitoring to 'avoid failure' and shame, escaping uncertain evaluation and self-acceptance
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, weakened passion for music, relationship tension with audience and peers, professional performance affected
